name: Fermilab E288
notes: Date conflicts: (1) start of the MuMu2 run - the Fermilab history page and one line of the 1977 Village Crier say 15 May 1977, another Crier line says 17 May; chosen 15 May. (2) The paper - Fermilab says it was submitted to PRL on 1 July 1977 and published in the 1 August 1977 issue; Lederman's lecture says "a paper was sent off in August of 1977"; the APS page says published 1 August 1977, which is used.

The predecessor E70 (proposal submitted 17 June 1970 and approved) is not an Atlas record; for the integrator: a lineage row can be added if E70 is created. The 400 GeV Main Ring is not an Atlas accelerator record, so accelerator_ids is empty.

The collaboration record is created because the bar asks for one where a collaboration exists (the brief did not list it); the integrator may drop it. Lederman is named spokesman on the Fermilab pages; no person records are created.

physics_goals.locator: Fermilab History and Archives, 'July 1, 1977: Discovery of the bottom quark'
physics_goals.quote: The experiment sought to study the rare events that occur when a proton beam collides with a platinum target, producing a pair of muons or electrons.
physics_goals.value: Study the rare events in which a proton beam on a platinum target produces a pair of muons or electrons

summary.plain: Leon Lederman's Columbia-Fermilab-Stony Brook team fired Fermilab's 400 GeV protons at a target and studied pairs of muons that came out. In 1977 they saw a bump at 9.5 GeV: the upsilon, the first sign of the bottom quark.
summary.technical: Dimuon spectrometer with 30 feet of beryllium hadron absorber and 2% mass resolution in 400 GeV p-nucleus collisions; the MuMu2 phase began taking data on 15 May 1977 and a 9.5 GeV resonance was announced on 30 June 1977 and published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 39, 252 (1 August 1977).

unique_capabilities.quote: A new rearrangement of target, shielding, and detector elements concentrated on muon pairs but with hadronic absorption being carried out in beryllium, actually 30 feet of beryllium.
unique_capabilities.value: Beryllium hadron absorber placed just after the target, so that the beam intensity could be raised
